title: Unfortunate interaction with libpq in client pipelining mode
body:
Hi!

We are trying to leverage benefits of libpq pipelining mode in https://github.com/userver-framework/userver, and we've managed to encounter a very unfortunate turn of events in production (we use odyssey as a bouncer), which goes like this:
```
> BDES (client sends bind, describe, execute, sync)
< EE (servers sends two errors)
```
The first error is from Postgres itself, "terminating connection due to administrator command", the second one is "remove server read/write error" from [odyssey](https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/blob/de02985941c0a375f9373aa78efd5abed56d44f7/sources/frontend.c#L1939).

------------------

The problem here is that the second error breaks libpq state-machine in the following scenario (in close-to-c pseudo-code):
```
PQenterPipelineMode(connection);    // entering pipeline mode
PQsendQueryPrepared(connection);    // buffers B, D, E
PQpipelineSync(connection);         // buffers S, flushes the BDES to the server

while (PQstatus(connection) != CONNECTION_BAD) {
   res = PQgetResult(connection);   // waits for the next result from the server
   if (PQresultStatus(res) == PGRES_PIPELINE_SYNC) {
       break;                       // current set of commands in the pipeline is processed
   }
}
```
like this https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/17948-fcace7557e449957%40postgresql.org (the loop above gets stuck in busy-loop)

---------------

I feel like it's libpq who is at fault here, but if not for the second **E**, which odyssey sends on its own, the `PQgetResult` call would detect the connection being closed and thus the loop would terminate.

I'm not 100% certain in my understanding of libpq and i could be mistaken/misusing libpq, but even if i'm not this is still mostly for reference and for whomever encounters the same behavior.

body:
In some PostgreSQL systems user permissions are not granted explicitly, they use `ROLE` session variable instead. For instance: `ALTER USER <login_user> SET ROLE <permission role>`. When Odyssey is in "smart_discard" mode and returns a connection to the pool, several statements are executed, including `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION DEFAULT`. This causes the session `ROLE` variable to reset to "none", resulting in the loss of its initial value:
```
2023-04-14 14:19:40 UTC [1326951] => [501-1] client=127.0.0.1,db=<db>,user=<user> LOG:  duration: 0.160 ms  statement: SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION DEFAULT;RESET ALL;CLOSE ALL;UNLISTEN *;SELECT pg_advisory_unlock_all();DISCARD PLANS;DISCARD SEQUENCES;DISCARD TEMP;
```
I think Odyssey developers used all statements that execute when `DISCARD ALL` happens and removed `DEALLOCATE ALL` from them and thus `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION DEFAULT` is also executed. After this statement is executed the session `ROLE` variable resets to `none` and its initial values is lost.
The new settings `pool_no_reset_auth` allows to skip `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION DEFAULT` statement in smart discard mode.
```
2023-04-14 14:18:48 UTC [1326725] => [496-1] client=127.0.0.1,db=<db>,user=<db> LOG:  duration: 0.103 ms  statement: RESET ALL;CLOSE ALL;UNLISTEN *;SELECT pg_advisory_unlock_all();DISCARD PLANS;DISCARD SEQUENCES;DISCARD TEMP;
```
This setting should be used in tandem with `smart_discard`. When both `smart_discard` and `pool_no_reset_auth` are enabled `SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION DEFAULT` will not be executed when Odyssey returns connection to the pool.

body:
Some drivers, for example [pgx v4](github.com/jackc/pgx/), have an error, because of which they can send a query twice without waiting for a response to the first queries. This is perceived by odyssey as switching to pipeline mode, and as a result, reading the response from the first query, pgx returns incorrect data (v4 doesn't support pipeline mode).

* PostgreSQL 11
* 5.10.0-21-amd64 #1 SMP Debian 5.10.162-1 (2023-01-21) x86_64 GNU/Linux
* GCP hosts - Machine type: e2-medium (2 core 4GB) or e2-standard-4 (4 core and 16Gb)

2) { | app | } <==> { | pgbouncer | <==> | HAproxy | <==>  | PostgreSQL | }

title: "Prepared statement does not exist" errors in transaction mode
body:
We're observing errors `prepared statement does not exist` in the applications that are connecting via odyssey to yugabyte db in transaction pool mode.

Example: 
```
org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: ERROR: prepared statement "2caa56bd" does not exist
```

The clients use pgjdbc to connect to odyssey.
The odyssey config for the db-user pair has the following settings,

```
pool "transaction"
pool_discard no
pool_smart_discard yes
pool_reserve_prepared_statement yes
```

The errors go away if we set `pool_reserve_prepared_statement` and `pool_smart_discard` to `no`. 

Are we missing anything in the configuration?

If we just disable server side prepared statements in jdbc by specifying `prepareThreshold=0` (and with `pool_reserve_prepared_statement yes` in odyssey config), then that doesn't help. Hence I am guessing that odyssey is getting these errors which it's relaying to the jdbc clients. Please correct me if I'm wrong.

Versions: 
Odyssey: built from this commit f4f60bc16c359af206c5a71c69fca5727fb2c40f
pgjdbc: 42.3.1

title: Bugs  autocommit
body:
This PR is regarding the issue: https://github.com/yandex/odyssey/issues/459
In the case of the `Multi-Query` transaction (or `AutoCommit=false`, the client application received the following error when it use the prepared statements.
```
org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: Expected command status BEGIN, got INSERT 0 1.
        at org.postgresql.core.v3.QueryExecutorImpl$1.handleCommandStatus(QueryExecutorImpl.java:620)
        at org.postgresql.core.v3.QueryExecutorImpl.interpretCommandStatus(QueryExecutorImpl.java:2720)
        at org.postgresql.core.v3.QueryExecutorImpl.processResults(QueryExecutorImpl.java:2313)
        at org.postgresql.core.v3.QueryExecutorImpl.execute(QueryExecutorImpl.java:355)
        at org.postgresql.jdbc.PgStatement.executeInternal(PgStatement.java:490)
        at org.postgresql.jdbc.PgStatement.execute(PgStatement.java:408)
        at org.postgresql.jdbc.PgPreparedStatement.executeWithFlags(PgPreparedStatement.java:167)
        at org.postgresql.jdbc.PgPreparedStatement.executeUpdate(PgPreparedStatement.java:135)
        at com.yugabyte.WriteTest.TestExtendedQuery(PerfTest.java:387)
        at com.yugabyte.WriteTest.run(PerfTest.java:429)
        at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:833)
```

When protocol level prepare statement is used the `statement_id` present in the [parse packet](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/protocol-message-formats.html#:~:text=of%20the%20parameter.-,Parse,-(F)) or [bind packet](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/protocol-message-formats.html#:~:text=of%20this%20backend.-,Bind,-(F)) is updated.
New `BIND` and `PARSE` packets are created by odyssey and sent to the server connection immediately; while for all other packets it forwarding takes a delay of one loop (odyssey packet processing loop).
This causes a `mismatch in the sequence of the packets sent to the server`.
In this workaround, all other packets(except `BIND` or `PARSE` which are modified) are also sent immediately (similar to `BIND` or `PARSE`) packets.

title: Problem with servers connection from odyssey through HAproxy
body:
Hi! First of all thanks for this product.

Second.

We have installation with Odyssey <---> HAproxy <---> PostgreSQL.
After switch app to odyssey we recived a lot of strange errors like

```
T13:02:05Z info [cb47523521fcb sb7656329d4c1] (main) server disconnected (read/write error): Broken pipe, status OD_ESERVER_WRITE
```
and
```
T13:15:05Z info [c56515b274f34 sa0a3bb0e2c20] (main) server disconnected (read/write error): Resource temporarily unavailable, status OD_ESERVER_READ
```
which broke query flow and crush our app.

And we found problem in HAproxy configuration which affect to Odyssey and create (from my point of view) strang Odyssey behavior.

If we have HAproxy client\server timeout 
```
defaults
    mode                    tcp
    log                     global
    retries                 2
    timeout queue           5s
    timeout connect         20s
    timeout client          60m
    timeout server          60m
    timeout check           20s
```

After 60 minut HAproxy send tcp-fin to Odyssey and it... must close connetion? or handel that somehow?
In pgbconsole i see that Odyssey just forget where it must sent packages (addr, port), but it doesn't close "logical" server connection.
And after then client try use connect to server connection and fallen.

*Red squares in the place where the connections just disappeared*
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43170236/199239471-1d7c4005-33e6-4b50-aff3-6956c87a71f3.png)


We tryed to user pool_ttl, but we still catch this situation. But more complexive.

```
database "database" {
        user "postgres" {
                authentication "clear_text"
                password "password"
                storage "storage_name.database"
                storage_db "postgres"
                storage_user "postgres"
                storage_password "password"
                pool "session"
                pool_size 60
                pool_timeout 0
                pool_ttl 60
                pool_cancel yes
                pool_rollback yes
                pool_discard yes
                client_fwd_error yes
                log_debug no
        }
    }
```

If we have one "broken" connection in pool, and amount connection is 5. 
And client sometimes use one connection from pool,  "broken" connection didn't closed and it can broke query flow When the load rises. 

Looks like pool_ttl it's timer for whole pool and not for separate server connection.



In general, so far we have not found an iron solution for this problem and I have not found similar cases in issues.

title: Fix undefined behaviour in od_worker_pool_feed function
body:
Currently od_worker_pool_feed function uses non-atomic access to
pool->round_robin variable. But od_worker_pool_feed function can be
called multiple time simultaneously from od_system_server, as odyssey
supports multiple listen addresses feauture, and no synchronization is
performed between concurrent listen coroutines. This entails data race, which
leads undefined behaviour in C/C++

title: Target session attr feature for storage

Storage host section is now accepts a comma-separated
PostgreSQL hosts list, in format "host2,host2"
or "[host1]:port1,host2" etc.

Storage structure now holds pointer to host, which connection was acquired.
This is required to cancel`s queries to work fine.

Target session attrs policies added:

* read-write
* read-only
* any (default)

Target session attrs uses pg_is_in_recovery function to
check if host in primary or replica. in_hot_standby option is not checked yet.

title: Format string bugs in od_logger_format
Add aarch64 support for machinarium context switch function
body:
Implement mm_context_swap function for AArch64 (64-bit ARM) architecture.
The purpose of mm_context_swap is to save all caller-safe registers to stack, then save stack pointer to arg0, and  change stack pointer to arg1. After stack pointer is changed, registers are popped back, `restoring` new running context.
Then we need to return somewhere, executing `ret` asm cmd. The return address should point to new context running function. 

That is, we enter mm_context_swap function in one coroutine and exit in other (not the same). 

On x86_64 or i386 architecture this is enforced by placing return address directly on stack  in context.c:37. The newly allocated stack will pop zero values to its registers and then execute ret cmd, returing to adrees is current stack pointer contains. 

On AArch64 `ret` command works in a different way: it returns to address stored in some register, x30 for default. This is why `mm_context_prepare` behaves differently in this case: we place return address to `*(sp + 1) `, this is exactly address which will be in x30 registers after context creation and block of `ldp` commands


The 64-bit ARM (AArch64) calling convention allocates the 31 general-purpose registers.

x31 (SP) is a stack pointer, we dont need to save in during `mm_context_swap_function`. 

Saved during `mm_context_prepare`:
x30 is procedure link register, x29 frame pointer, we need to store them, also we need to save x19 to x29, which is callee-saved registers. 
x18 is platform register, x16 and x17 intra-procedure-call scratch registers, i decided its better to save them then not.
x8 indirect return value address, i thick its better to save such thing.

Not saved during `mm_context_prepare`:
x9 to x15: Local variables, caller saved, so dont need to save on stack.
x0 to x7: Argument values passed to and results returned from a subroutine, we dont save them.

Add docker images wich odyssey test on Aarch64, also provide some deb-packages

title: Access management to PostgreSQL with LDAP
body:
Dear maintainers @reshke @x4m !

I want to extend functionality of ldap authentication for strict access between different users to different databases on same host.
For example, we have a user "user1" who must access to database "applications" with readonly permissions (SELECT only).
And also user "user1" must access to database "proposals" with a read-write permissions (for example, SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE).
In a current way for give this permissions to database with a connection throught odyssey we need construct config like that:
```
storage "test_server" {
    host "test-server-for-ldap"
}
database "applications" {
    user "user1" {
            storage "test_server"
            storage_user "readonly-user"
            storage_password "password"            
            storage_db  "applications"
    }  
}
database "proposals" {
    user "user1" { 
            storage "test_server"
            storage_user "readwrite-user"
            storage_password "password"            
            storage_db  "proposals"
    }   
}
````
But in real environments may be too much count of users and different database on same host.
And if we going on that way - config would be not readble.

So I want to introduce a way for solve this problem with ldap authorization:
when odyssey connect to ldap for authenticate a user, after suceess authentication odyssey may receive from
ldap-server optional attributes of this user. For example it's may be a Groups.
And if we construct name of this Groups with a rules thats contains host, database and storage_user then
we can route user connection throught odyssey with a simple config, for example:

```
storage "test_server" {
    host "test-server-for-ldap"
}

ldap_endpoint "ldap1" {
}

database "default" {
    user "default" {
            storage "test_server"
            storage_user "readonly-user"
            storage_password "*******"            
            storage_db  "applications"
            ldap_endpoint_name "ldap1"

            ldap_storage_user_attr "memberof"

            ldap_storage_user "group_ro" {
                ldap_storage_username "ldap_ro"
                ldap_storage_password "password"
            }

            ldap_storage_user "group_rw" {
                ldap_storage_username "ldap_rw"
                ldap_storage_password "password"
            }
     }
}
```
For example, if we wants to grant access to "user1" with readonly permissions to database "trade_offers" -
just need to invite "user1" to Group called "test-server-for-ldap_trade_offers_group_ro" on LDAP-server.


But in current state of this PR a have **problem** with a race between clients who connects to odyssey.
The problem is that in after first step of connection to odyssey open and close connection to Backend.
And if we have two clients in a pending state:
```
console=> show clients;
 type |  user   | database  |  state  |     addr      | port  | local_addr  | local_port | con 
------+---------+-----------+---------+---------------+-------+-------------+------------+-
 C    | root    | console   | pending | 127.0.0.1     | 48640 | 127.0.0.1   |       6432 |  
 C    | user1   | test-db1  | pending | 192.168.3.242 | 50976 | 172.17.1.88 |       6432 |   
 C    | user2   | test-db2  | pending | 192.168.3.242 | 50980 | 172.17.1.88 |       6432 |       

```
then first of clients who attach to backend will be use storage_user credential of last client who setup connection to backend 
(in od_frontend_setup_params).


I will be very appreciative if you could help me solve this problem.
In this case, I see 2 solutions:
1) somehow, when a client connects to the backend, update (or recheck) in the connection variables to the backend exactly those credentials that were received through ldap authorization
(in at that way I find how set password again, but I could not change username for connect to PostgreSQL)
2) after a successful first connection to the backend, do not close the connection, but transfer the client to the active state
(at least not to authenticate a second time)

I am building a new active-hotstandby database-setup with patroni. I intended to use pgbouncer (as the old setup had), but just now learned about this project. The big advantage of odyssey would be the way simpler implementation of ldap-auth.

Because i am working with patroni i relay on haproxy with routes the traffic to the current r/w host, it is doing so by watching patronis health-api.

My question: Is odyssey somehow able to handle two pg-servers in one backend and automatically route traffic to the current active node? If so, how? I did not see how this could be done in the docs... This would be a killer feature for us and we would switch from pgbouncer pretty soon i think :)
